GM Said They Can't Build a Manual C8 Corvette. These Guys Just Did!
8 photos
Photo: Alex Peitz | YouTube
General Motors said they can't, and they won't build a manual C8 Chevrolet Corvette. Well, Peitz Performance did it. They entirely reengineered the car to make room for a manual six-speed transaxle and invited the Shelby American president to do donuts in it.
The last time the Chevrolet Corvette lineup featured a factory manual transmission was the 2019 model year, which marked the end of the seventh-generation C7 production. The final Corvette with a gear shifter was a black 2019 Z06 coupe , featuring a seven-speed manual that rolled off the production line of the Bowling Green Assembly Plant in Kentucky on November 14, 2019. The model was later auctioned off for charity for $2.7 million.
When the mid-engine eighth generation launched for the 2020 model year, Chevrolet eliminated the manual option entirely due to structural design constraints and low consumer demand, which had dropped by roughly 22% by 2019. The current lineup relies exclusively on the Tremec dual-clutch automatic transmission.
Furthermore, earlier this year, C8 Corvette executive chief engineer Tony Roma shut down rumors about a potential manual transmission when rumors started making the rounds after Tremec displayed a manual transmission at SEMA in late 2025.
Photo: Alex Peitz | YouTube While General Motors went on the "no can do" strategy, Peitz Performance came out saying, "Oh, yes, we can!" Because the C8 Corvette is engineered around the eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, building a true manual required re-engineering the car.
Peitz Performance used a Tremec-built, brand-new TR-9060 six-speed manual transaxle, designed to handle up to 1,000 pound-feet of torque and adapt the differential right from the C8’s stock dual-clutch housing.
The transmission is operated with the help of a custom cable-driven shifter , heavily modified from a Porsche aftermarket setup. To give the driver a third pedal, Peitz integrated a modified clutch assembly, taken straight from a Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing.
The biggest hurdle was the car’s computer. The Peitz engineers managed to bypass GM’s locked factory setup, using a high-end MoTeC M182 plug-and-play ECU, paired with an M150 TCU. The setup allows the car to run flawlessly without dashboard error codes, while enabling downshift throttle blips and automatic upshift ignition cuts.
Photo: Alex Peitz | YouTube To prove what the manual Corvette can do, Peitz Performance invited the President of Shelby American to see what it can do. Gary Patterson crossed the enemy lines, took the manual 'Vette for a spin and did donuts in it.
Peitz Performance lists the complete turn-key conversion package at a staggering $74,528.999. The specialized MoTeC electronics alone drive a huge portion of that price. But as the company is still working on the electronics, customer availability is slated for July 2027.
You must provide the C8 Corvette yourself. This means that a Corvette Stingray with a row-your-own gearbox is roughly $148,000. In the meantime, manual-swapping a brand-new Corvette ZR1X would push the cost into extreme hypercar territory, putting your total expected investment at roughly $302,000.
